text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Opposition Liberal party deputy leader Anders Fogh Rasmussen urges the Conservatives not to enter into a pact with the minority Social Democrat-led government on next year's state budget, warning that such a move would damage the chances of forming a Liberal-Conservative alliance to fight Denmark's next elections in 1998.

--- Copenhagen authorities are working on a new local plan to oust Hell's Angels bikers from their headquarters in a built-up central area of the capital and turn the building over to public use. The plan should make it impossible for the bikers to stay on in their headquarters after this weekend's missile attack which killed two people and wounded 19.

--- A new Sonar survey shows that less than half of all Danish voters support social welfare cuts, despite the fact that three out of four voters feel that far too many Danes receive public benefits. Voter support centres on early retirement benefits, student grants and pension schemes while a large group want cutbacks in state-paid leave, housing and cash benefits.

--- Foreign insurance companies are taking over a large chunk of the Danish domestic market for business insurance, causing problems for local insurance companies which unlike foreign competitors cannot offer global insurance policies.
